title: Zipline Launches First Flight Drone Delivery Program in Austin
source_used: Unite.AI (article relaying a Zipline announcement; its byline is an AI-generated author)
key_facts: Zipline launched its First Flight early-access program in Austin on 9 Oct 2026, open to the first 5,000 residents who register; service starts in Round Rock.
Members get $10 off each of their first three orders and pay no service or delivery fees.
The drone flies to the address, hovers above 300 feet and lowers a pod on a tether; the full delivery sequence takes about 90 seconds, Zipline says.
Zipline says a software update gave a 30% reduction in perceived noise and calls its system six times quieter during delivery than others in the industry.
Zipline says its drones have flown more than 140 million miles and completed more than 3 million deliveries, in more than 30 municipalities in four US states.
Zipline cites TomTom data that Austin commutes took 40% longer than free-flow travel in 2025.
quote_evidence: Zipline launched its First Flight early-access program in Austin on October 9, 2026, opening autonomous drone delivery to the first 5,000 residents who register.
On arrival, the aircraft hovers above 300 feet while a tether lowers a pod carrying the order to the ground.
why_it_matters_hint: Drone delivery moves from other cities into the Austin area, with noise the main public question.
notes: The Unite.AI page says its author is an AI-generated research agent reviewed by editors. All performance and quietness figures are Zipline's own claims. Round Rock is in Williamson County (county judge quoted).
